assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's 2003 proposal of magic-wavelength optical lattices and the subsequent demonstrations opened the door to clocks with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and below. This is a new measurement tool that makes previously unseeable effects measurable, such as gravitational redshift over millimetres, and it is the platform for tests of fundamental constants and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: The lattice-clock concept is clearly Katori's. Ye's group made the decisive demonstrations of record accuracy and stability, including the strontium clock and the many-body clock. The two-name configuration is tight and easy to defend. Others such as Lemonde, Ludlow and Hinkley contributed, but the original idea and the leading experiments are well localised.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups at JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and elsewhere over two decades, with international clock comparisons. The result is stable and mature; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Hänsch/Hall (2005) and Wineland (2012) precedent leaves room for a further precision-timekeeping prize is a committee judgement.
Precise priority between lattice-clock variants (Sr, Yb, Hg) is not independently verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle bilayer graphene, created the moire quantum-materials field. The discovery is a prediction confirmed by a decisive experiment, and it has spawned a very large body of verified work on tunable correlated states.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery (with Yuan Cao as lead student). Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the original theory. The three-name set fits one theory plus one experiment. Possible disputes over other contributors, such as Dean/Hone on moire devices and other early theory, should be acknowledged.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups in several moire platforms within a few years. The physics of the superconductivity is still debated, but the existence of the phenomena is well established. Possibly slightly early but the field is already mature in experimental terms.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of superconductivity is unresolved.
Extent to which other early theory work should share credit is uncertain.
Whether the prize should wait for application outcomes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall state by Kane and Mele and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group opened topological insulators as a new class of matter, with robust edge conduction that was verified by transport. It is an original theory-plus-experiment pair of very large impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the central theoretical proposals; Molenkamp led the HgTe quantum-well experiment, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicting the HgTe route. That omission is a real attribution problem within a three-person limit, and the competing 3D topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan) complicates the picture.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple experiments and extensively developed; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Molenkamp and the 3D topological insulator discoverers is unresolved.
Compound discovery: 2D and 3D parts may require different treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: a designed intersubband laser whose emission wavelength is set by layer thickness, not by the bandgap, demonstrated in 1994. It opened mid-infrared and terahertz sources for sensing, spectroscopy and applications that benefit society. This is a clear invention with real-world impact.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso led the first demonstration at Bell Labs, and Cho's molecular-beam epitaxy growth was essential. Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson and Kazarinov (earlier 1971 proposal with Suris) are also relevant, so the three-name choice is defensible but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and widely replicated for three decades; thoroughly mature and long overdue in timing.
uncertainties: Credit for the 1971 Kazarinov-Suris proposal versus the 1994 realisation.
Whether the committee regards it as physics rather than engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pendry's theory of negative refraction, the perfect lens and structures with engineered permeability, together with Smith's first experimental demonstration of a negative-index medium, opened a door to controlling light and waves at will. The first demonstration is the original experiment that I look for.
assessment.attribution: Pendry provided the theoretical framework and Smith led the first experimental realisation with Schultz and Shelby. Veselago's 1968 prediction is a historical predecessor but is not in the credit list. Capasso (metasurfaces) is a later, distinct development and I would keep it separate.
assessment.maturity: Negative refraction has been replicated at microwave and optical frequencies; applications such as cloaking and superlensing are less mature and the perfect-lens limit is debated. Interpretation is stable but practical impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Impact on humanity beyond science is moderate so far.
Priority issues between microwave and optical demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire (Moulton) and Kerr-lens mode-locking (Sibbett's group), together with Keller's semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors, made reliable solid-state femtosecond lasers. These are enabling instruments for attosecond physics, spectroscopy and frequency combs. As a tools-that-open-doors candidate it fits the committee's interest, and the 2018 chirped-pulse prize and 2023 attosecond prize have already recognised neighbouring areas.
assessment.attribution: Three distinct decisive inventions: Ti:sapphire gain medium (Moulton), Kerr-lens mode-locking (Sibbett and colleagues, Spence), and SESAM (Keller). Credit boundaries are messy since Spence, Kean and Sibbett's paper is the Kerr-lens one. Keller is a woman, which is consistent with encouraging recognition of women, though that is not a criterion for me.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature, widely used and independently validated for over three decades.
uncertainties: Overlap with already recognised ultrafast optics prizes may weaken novelty.
Exact priority for Kerr-lens mode-locking is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED (2004 theory by Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf with Huang, Girvin and colleagues; experiment by Wallraff et al.) gave a way to read out and couple superconducting qubits via microwave resonators and underlies present quantum processors. It is an enabling measurement architecture with strong experimental verification.
assessment.attribution: Wallraff and Schoelkopf's groups carried out the decisive experiment and Blais contributed to the theory, with Girvin as co-author of the key paper and a notable omission from the supplied set. Allocation is a recognised unresolved matter. The 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits touches the same field, which may affect timing.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and now the basis of commercial quantum computing efforts. Mature.
uncertainties: Credit for Girvin and Devoret and the relation to the 2025 prize.
Prize may be viewed as too soon after related recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental realisation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped topological insulator films (2013) demonstrated quantised Hall resistance without an external field, a decisive experimental advance with prior theory by Haldane and Fang/Dai. It is an experiment where the original observation is clear.
assessment.attribution: Xue's group did the decisive experiment; Dai and Fang predicted the Cr-doped route. Haldane (1988) is not on the list, and Chang and Moodera's related work needs consideration. Precision metrology follow-ups (Goldhaber-Gordon, Zhang group) complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by several groups, though operating temperatures are low and the effect is delicate. Interpretation is stable. A combined topological insulator prize could reasonably subsume this.
uncertainties: Overlap with the topological insulator candidate.
Haldane's earlier concept and the Chang/Moodera contribution may require acknowledgement.
Whether it is separable from the quantum spin Hall prize.
